name: Knorri (Hörri)
description: Knorri (also known as HÃ¶rri) is a traditional Finnish card game for three to eight players. It belongs to the 'beating' or 'avoidance' family of games (like Skitgubbe). The game is uniquely divided into two phases: a 'Collection Phase' where cards are picked up from the table based on rank-matching, and a 'Trick Phase' where players must play the cards they collected to avoid being the last person with cards in hand.

content.text: Knorri (also known as HÃ¶rri) is a traditional Finnish card game for three to eight players. It belongs to the 'beating' or 'avoidance' family of games (like Skitgubbe). The game is uniquely divided into two phases: a 'Collection Phase' where cards are picked up from the table based on rank-matching, and a 'Trick Phase' where players must play the cards they collected to avoid being the last person with cards in hand.
Originates in Finland, likely derived from the Swedish game 'Mas' or 'Skitgubbe'. The name 'Knorri' is localized Finnish slang for the rhythmic flipping of cards.
Standard 52-card deck. Diamonds are **Trumps**. Clubs are **Hard/Anti-Trump** (Anti-Truff).

No cards are dealt to players. 9 cards are placed face-up on the table to start. The rest form a draw pile.

items.text: Soft clubs: Clubs can be beaten by any spade, heart or diamond; diamonds trump all, hearts and spades trump clubs, clubs beat only lower clubs.
Scoring: Optional scoring: +1 per player still in when you go out; loser gets negative points so total is zero (e.g. 4-player: +3, +2, +1, -6).
Last Card: Player with one card must announce "last card" before next player plays; forgetting forces them to take bottom card of trick on next turn instead of going out.
